final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest phenotype score (0.980) at the catalytic lysine that forms the PLP internal aldimine; threonine substitution abolishes the catalytic Lys. Low PLM plausibility is consistent with a damaging, activity-abolishing mutation.
Very high phenotype score (0.912) at conserved catalytic Cys103 in the CxxH/CxxxC motif; bulky tyrosine disrupts the catalytic cysteine and the active-site architecture.
Strong phenotype score (0.878) at conserved Cys52 of the catalytic motif; tyrosine substitution eliminates the catalytic cysteine side chain, abolishing activity.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence is consistent and decisive across phenotype, MSA, and PLM tools; further calls would not change the final Top-3.

history.rationale: Cys52 is the axial heme ligand in human CBS; substitution with bulky Tyr disrupts heme coordination, a classic loss-of-function mechanism seen in homocystinuria alleles.
Cys52 is a key catalytic residue forming the internal PLP-lysine aldimine partner; substitution with bulky Tyr should abolish activity. Retained pending evidence.

High pathogenicity (0.878) and near-zero evolutionary tolerance of Y at position 52; C52 is part of the heme-binding region critical for CBS stability/activity. PLM implausibility is expected for a damaging mutation and is not contradictory to the LOF goal.
Strong phenotype score (0.878) at a conserved catalytic cysteine; tyrosine substitution abolishes the Cys-Lys catalytic pair.
His65 is the second axial heme ligand; alanine at this position ablates heme binding and abolishes CBS activity while being structurally tolerated.
His65 acts as a general base in the beta-replacement reaction; alanine substitution should eliminate catalysis while preserving fold.
Pathogenicity 0.845 supports damaging effect, but slightly below C103Y and K119T; retained as reserve. Low MSA tolerance of A at 65 supports disruption.
Decent phenotype score (0.845) at catalytic His65, but alanine is less disruptive than Cys/Tyr swaps; remains backup.
Lys119 forms the internal Schiff base with PLP; even the conservative K-to-R change eliminates PLP anchoring and catalytic turnover.
Lys119 is the PLP-binding lysine forming the Schiff base; conservative-looking K→R still abolishes PLP attachment because the longer side chain cannot form the aldimine correctly.
Conservative substitution (K→R) with the lowest phenotype score of the catalytic-site candidates (0.777); demoted. Retained as backup only.
Conservative Lys->Arg retains positive charge at the catalytic lysine and may partially preserve function; demoted below H65A.
Thr at the PLP-anchoring lysine removes the Schiff-base chemistry entirely, yielding a catalytically dead but fold-competent enzyme.
Same PLP-lysine target as K119R with a non-basic replacement; slightly less confident on structural integrity of the PLP pocket.

alphamissense 0.980 is the strongest LOF proxy in the pool; low MSA frequency of T at 119 confirms the site is not evolutionarily tolerant. K119 (active-site lysine in the PLP/Cys-Persulfide catalytic region) mutation is mechanistically sound for abolishing activity.
Highest phenotype score (0.980) targeting the catalytic lysine; low PLM plausibility is expected for a damaging catalytic mutation and reinforces LOF.
Cys103 lies in the heme-proximal cysteine-rich region; a bulky Tyr perturbs heme pocket geometry and impairs activity.
Cys103 is near the PLP pocket; possible functional disruption but mechanism less certain than Lys119/His65 hits.

alphamissense 0.912 and mutant frequency 0.023 support strong damaging effect; Cys103 is a conserved cysteine whose substitution is well tolerated as a LOF mechanism. Raised above H65A and K119R on phenotype evidence.
Very high phenotype score (0.912) at conserved Cys103 in the catalytic core; bulkier aromatic substitution likely disrupts fold and activity.
Cys109 is adjacent to the heme-ligating cysteines; serine substitution alters the local redox/heme environment and reduces catalytic function.
Cys109 is a cysteine-rich-region residue; C→S is mild and may not abolish activity, kept as a lower-tier candidate.

C→S is a mild cysteine substitution with the weakest overall support (phenotype 0.876 but serine retains some chemical character); PLM and MSA offer no distinguishing support. Dropped to keep the pool focused on stronger LOF candidates.

rejection.reason: C→S is a mild cysteine substitution with the weakest overall support (phenotype 0.876 but serine retains some chemical character); PLM and MSA offer no distinguishing support. Dropped to keep the pool focused on stronger LOF candidates.
